title: tui-tools tool manifest
description: The tool.json every tui-tools repository carries at its root. It is the single source the family website reads to build a tool's card and detail page.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema the manifest was written against.

name.description: The tool name, which is also the repository name: tui-<target>, no aliases.

binary.description: The installed executable. Same as name for every tool in the family.

tagline.description: One line for the marketplace card. No trailing period.

description.description: A short paragraph or two for the detail page. A safe subset of markdown: paragraphs, `code`, **bold**, _italic_ and [links](url). No headings, no images, no HTML.

category.description: The single shelf this tool sits on in the marketplace grid.

homepage.description: Where a human should be sent to read about the tool.

platforms.description: The os/arch pairs a release ships binaries for.

icon.description: Repository-relative path to the tool icon, preferably SVG.

logo.description: Repository-relative path to the horizontal lockup, optional.

screenshots.description: Ordered gallery. The first one is the card thumbnail, so make it the opening screen.

caption.description: Alt text and gallery caption. Describe what the frame shows.

keys.description: The shortcuts worth advertising, not the full help screen.

install.description: How to get the tool, one entry per package manager. Every entry carries a real command even when `available` is false: a channel that is not published yet is shown as coming soon, with the command it will be, rather than hidden.

security.description: The promises the family makes, answered for this tool. The website renders it as a checklist, so every field is deliberate.

needs_sudo.description: What the tool escalates for, in one sentence. false when it never escalates.

preview_before_run.description: Every mutation is shown as an exact command line and confirmed first. The family contract: it must be true.

no_daemon.description: Nothing keeps running after you quit, and nothing is installed to run later.

no_network.description: The tool opens no network connection of its own.

no_network_note.description: Required when no_network is false: what it talks to, and why.

static_binary.description: Released as a statically linked binary, no runtime dependencies.

signed_releases.description: Release artifacts carry a signature beyond the SHA-256 checksums file.

config_paths.description: Every path the tool reads or writes for its own configuration, in precedence order.

since.description: The date the tool was first published, YYYY-MM-DD.

keywords.description: Extra search terms for the website. Repository topics are a good source.

unreleased.description: Set to true for a tool that deliberately has no release yet, such as the template.

available.description: true when the package can be installed today. false renders as "coming soon" — the command is still shown, so a reader knows what it will be.

package.description: The package name in this manager's namespace, when it differs from the tool name (an AUR -bin package, say).

repo.description: The repository the package comes from: a repo id for pacman/apt/dnf/zypper ("tui-tools"), or "aur".

command.description: The shell line a reader copies, assuming the one-time repository setup has been done. Placeholders {version} and {arch} are expanded against the latest release.

requires_repo_setup.description: true when the command only works after the family repository has been added — the site links to /install/ for the one-time setup.

pattern.description: Release asset name with {version} and {arch} placeholders. The binary channel uses it to build direct download links.

url.description: Where the package lives, or where it will.

note.description: One line of context shown under the command.
